title: PBL Builder Project Plan
description: A Gold Standard PBL project designed for one specific learner. Lives in the YAML frontmatter of a project-plan.md. The body of that file carries the required headings: Project Summary, Why This Project For This Learner, Week-by-Week Plan, Notes & Adaptations.

title.description: A name the learner would actually say out loud. 'The Creek Project' beats 'Grade 4 Watershed Interdisciplinary Unit'.

slug.description: kebab-case. Matches the containing folder name.

status.description: `reviewed` means it has passed `pbl review` with no failures. `abandoned` is a legitimate outcome worth recording — see Notes & Adaptations.

learner_profile.description: Relative path to the learner-profile.md this plan was designed from. Required — a plan with no profile behind it is the failure mode this repo exists to prevent. `pbl review` reads it to check profile fidelity.

driving_question.description: Open-ended, in language this learner would use, and answerable only by learning the target standards. `pbl review` checks its shape. See docs/07-driving-questions.md.

assessed_by.description: Which product or assessment provides evidence for this standard. If you can't name one, the standard isn't really in the project.

understandings.description: What you want them to still understand in a year, in your own words. Bigger than any single standard.

success_skill.description: EXACTLY ONE skill, with the specific dimensions being taught. Everything else on that rubric is explicitly out of scope for this project.

taught_how.description: How the skill gets explicitly TAUGHT, not just assessed. This is the field people skip, and skipping it is why success skills don't grow.

context.description: The real-world situation this mirrors. Whose job looks like this?

real_world_processes.description: Actual tools, methods, and quality standards from that world.

impact.description: What could genuinely change because this work exists. 'Nothing, but it's realistic' is an honest answer — write that instead of inventing impact.

personal_connection.description: MUST name a specific interest from the learner profile. `pbl review` check 9 verifies this — 'connects to student interests' will fail. Name the interest.

products.description: What the learner makes. In a solo context one strong product beats three thin ones.

who.description: Real people beyond the household or tutoring pair. Name them. 'The community' is not an audience; 'the watershed council's monthly meeting' is.

date.description: Target date. Set it early — it's what makes the deadline real.

comfort_ramp.description: Graduated rehearsal audiences for a learner with low audience_comfort: one trusted adult → small friendly group → the real audience. Required by `pbl review` when the profile says audience_comfort is low. This is the alternative to dropping the public product — never do that.

backup_plan.description: What happens if the audience falls through. It sometimes does.

voice_and_choice.description: Real decisions the learner makes — the kind an adult professional would make. Choosing the font colour is not voice and choice.

product.description: Choices about what to make and for whom.

calibrated_for.description: Must match the profile's preferences.choice_appetite. `pbl review` check 11.

widens_when.description: For a low-appetite learner: what has to happen before you offer more choice. Choice should grow during the project.

description.description: The hook. Something seen, done, or visited — not a topic announcement. Design it so the questions you want naturally get asked.

anticipated_ntk.description: Questions you expect the learner to raise. If your list doesn't overlap the standards, the entry event is pointing the wrong way.

project_path.description: All four phases, always. See framework/project-path.yaml.

scaffolds.description: Supports selected for THIS learner's needs. Every populated need tag in the profile must be addressed by at least one scaffold (`pbl review` check 9), and every scaffold must have a fade plan (check 10).

id.description: Scaffold id from framework/scaffolds.yaml, or a custom id if you invented one.

addresses.description: Which need tags from the profile this addresses.

fade_plan.description: How and when this support comes off. Required. A scaffold that never fades is a permanent accommodation — put those in the profile's needs.accommodations instead.

responds_how.description: What you'll DO with what you learn. Formative assessment you don't act on is just record-keeping.

formative.description: Must include checks in both build_knowledge and develop_and_critique (`pbl review` check 8).

criteria_from.description: Where the criteria come from — a rubric path, or the standards themselves.

who_assesses.description: Teacher, learner, peer, expert, audience, or several.

success_skill_checks.description: How growth on the ONE targeted skill gets checked, separately from content. Include at least one self-assessment — the skill rubrics are for the learner, not just you.

support_plan.description: Replaces classroom management in a one-learner setting. This is the section that determines whether week three holds together.

adult_role.description: What you do and, importantly, what you don't. 'I answer questions with questions until Thursday' is a real role.

check_in_cadence.description: How often you formally check in, and what happens in that check-in.

stuck_protocol.description: What happens when the learner stalls — the specific escalation, before it becomes a crisis. Required, because it always happens and improvising it goes badly.

critique_partners.description: Who provides critique when there's no class. A sibling, a co-op, a grandparent, an online group, an expert, you in a different role. Name them — critique with nobody to give it doesn't happen.

when_to_stop.description: Your own tripwire for abandoning or reshaping the project. Worth deciding in advance, while you're calm.

texts_and_media.description: Sources the learner will use. Check these against their reading level.

type.description: A product type id from framework/product-types.yaml. `pbl review` check 9 verifies its modes overlap the learner's product_modes.

criteria.description: What makes it good. Derive these from the standards, not from neatness.

why_this_learner.description: Why THIS product for THIS learner. If you can't answer, you picked a product type off a list rather than for a person.

ntk_questions.description: What the learner needs to figure out here. Written as their question, not your objective.

scaffolds.description: Scaffold ids in play at this milestone.

reflection.description: A reflection prompt or protocol. `pbl review` check 7 wants at least two across at least two phases.

critique.description: A critique-and-revision cycle. At least one must occur before the present phase (check 6).

deliverable.description: What exists at the end of this milestone.
